examples.trans: Bring me a bottle of wine to the office.

examples.text: Федя, давай быстрее, захвати бутылку виски!
examples.trans: Fedya, hurry up, grab a bottle of whiskey!

examples.text: С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'wine', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Принесите мне бутылку вина в кабинет.
examples.trans: Bring me a bottle of wine to the office.

examples.text: Это очень хорошее вино.
examples.trans: This is very good wine.

examples.text: Бокал красного вина.
examples.trans: A glass of red wine.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: В следующий раз нож будет выше!
examples.trans: Next time the knife will be higher!

examples.text: Жду вас в восемь часов в Аркобалено.
examples.trans: I am waiting for you at eight o'clock at Arcobaleno.

examples.text: Да, конечно, вечером всё в силе!
examples.trans: Yes, of course, everything is still on for tonight!

meanings.note: From French 'cabinet' (private study or office).

examples.text: Принесите мне бутылку вина в кабинет.
examples.trans: Bring me a bottle of wine to the office.

examples.text: Я в кабинете.
examples.trans: I'm in the office.

examples.text: Это кабинет мэра.
examples.trans: This is the mayor's office.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Герман меня звал, какой он романтичный!
examples.trans: German called for me, how romantic he is!

examples.text: Как тебя зовут?
examples.trans: What's your name?

examples.text: Меня зовут Лёша.
examples.trans: My name is Lyosha.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Каких ещё леопардов, у меня же банкет!
examples.trans: What leopards, I have a banquet after all!

examples.text: Вы знаете, какая у нас недостача?
examples.trans: Do you know what a shortage we have?

examples.text: Герман меня звал, какой он романтичный!
examples.trans: German called for me, how romantic he is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('he') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Ещё утром я видела его в холодильнике.
examples.trans: Just this morning I saw it in the refrigerator.

examples.text: До его прихода такой недостачи не было.
examples.trans: Before his arrival there was no such shortage.

examples.text: Как он появился, сразу стали пропадать продукты!
examples.trans: As soon as he appeared, groceries immediately started disappearing!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'romantic', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Герман меня звал, какой он романтичный!
examples.trans: German called for me, how romantic he is!

examples.text: Мне сказали, вы хотели меня видеть.
examples.trans: I was told you wanted to see me.
